newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFIs show paper losses, but rebound seen.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFIs show paper losses, but rebound seen.

text.p: Most of Poland's 15 National Investment Funds (NFIs) showed heavy losses in 1996 largely due to accountancy operations, but should start showing profits this year, analysts said on Monday.

Jacek Koczwara of BGZ brokerage told Reuters the losses were a result of recalculation of depreciation for 1995 and the first nine months of 1996 which was based on gross rather than net value of assets.
"In most cases they are not losses at operating level but are caused by accountancy operations -- mainly recalculation of depreciation," he said.

Analysts said the losses were also due to companies selling their non-productive assets such as sports fields or vacation hotels for employees, often below their book value which was much higher than market value.
They said the companies in the funds' portfolios and the funds themselves were also making many kinds of provisions, which negatively influenced their profit and loss accounts.
According to unaudited results NFI 8 had a 72-million- zloty ($23.1 million) loss in 1996, NFI 1 46.5 million zlotys, NFI 14 had a net loss of 14.3 million zlotys and NFI 7 12.8 a million-zloty loss.
NFI 9 had a 4.2 million-zloty net profit after 9.5 million in 1995 and the remaining funds would report their 1996 earnings later this week.

Analysts said, however, that after the so-called cleaning of the companies' balances was completed and the accountancy operations finished, the funds' growth prospects were good and they expected a rebound in earnings in 1997.
"The process of managing the companies is just beginning; the whole programme is a long-term one and I wouldn't worry," Klaudiusz Wolny, deputy president of the Pioneer brokerage, told Reuters.

"The funds' financial results for 1997 have to be better, as some of their firms are approved for public trade, so part of their assets will be valued by the market and made real, which might cause a sudden change of financial parameters," he said.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in more than 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.

From May 12 the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme will have the opportunity to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund, which are expected to start trade on the Warsaw bourse around mid-year.
